title: Foundry stales 20 full-difficulty Bitcoin blocks that no observer saw
summary: Across September 11–12, 2025, Foundry USA produced 20 full-difficulty stale Bitcoin blocks across 16 heights (914,261–914,373), foregoing ~46.9 BTC and surviving only in RSK and Fractal AuxPoW captures.
body:
After an initial self-race at height `914,261`, Foundry staled 19 more full-difficulty blocks over ~17 hours across 15 further heights through `914,373` (13 attributed via parent coinbase tags, 7 via the RSK reward-address registry), losing ~46.9 BTC in races won by competing pools.[^1]

Cluster stale headers carry timestamps 6 to 1,621 seconds earlier than their canonical winners (median ~600s), and every stale builds on a canonical parent rather than chaining onto a prior stale—the signature of a recurring block-submission failure rather than a propagation race or chain split.[^1]

ForkMonitor and peer observers recorded none of these blocks, indicating they likely never propagated beyond the pool; the headers survive only because RSK and Fractal embedded the parent templates via AuxPoW.[^2]
